target_files.change_summary: Stage A: move <useTags>true</useTags> to be a direct child of <configOptions> and delete the <tags> wrapper (verified: today it is nested in <tags>, so it is ignored and only com.alramz.api.ApiApi is generated). Stage B: add spring-boot-starter-liquibase (BOM-managed), org.postgresql:postgresql (runtime), com.oracle.database.jdbc:ojdbc11 (runtime) and com.oracle.database.nls:orai18n (runtime), copying wealth-management-service/pom.xml. Change h2 from runtime to test scope. Keep spring-boot-starter-data-jpa, because the starter's JwtAutoConfiguration needs it (@EnableJpaRepositories com.alramz.jwt.repository). Do not add the liquibase-maven-plugin (optional CLI tooling, not needed). Stages C and D: extend modelsToGenerate, first with TemplatedEmailRequest,TemplateAttachment and then with SmsSendRequest,SmsSendResult,SmsRecipientResult,SmsReportResult, ending at the 10 models in spec 3.5.

Stage C: add POST /api/v1/email/template/send (operationId sendTemplatedEmail, tag TemplatedEmail) with responses 200/400 (EML001-006 plus MGE-V-005/006 examples)/401 (description only)/403/413/429/500/502, and schemas TemplatedEmailRequest and TemplateAttachment (content format: byte; x-field-extra-annotation @com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonAlias({"contenttype"}) / ({"filename"}), the feature 1 mechanism). Generalise the GenericResponse.errorCode and response descriptions. Stage D: add POST /api/v1/sms/send (sendSms, tag Sms; 200/400/401/403/500/502/503) and GET /api/v1/sms/report/{messageId} (getSmsReport, tag Sms; 200/400/401/403/404/500/502/503), plus the schemas SmsSendRequest (mobileNumbers alias mobileNumber), SmsSendResult, SmsRecipientResult and SmsReportResult (reports: array of object with additionalProperties string). Paths keep the full /api/v1 prefix, following the local precedent (verified: the existing path is /api/v1/email/send and no controller adds a class-level prefix). Verified that none of the new operationIds or schema names collide with existing ones.

@baseUrl, @authToken and the register/login blocks already exist (verified). Stage C: add '### Send Templated Email' (positive) and '### Send Templated Email -ve (unknown templateName, expects 400 EML002)'. Stage D: add '### Send SMS' (simulated mode) plus '### Send SMS -ve (invalid number, expects 400 SMS002)', and '### Get SMS Report' plus '### Get SMS Report -ve (messageId abc&pwd=x, expects 400 SMS007)'. Use only example.com addresses and 9715000000xx numbers. Place the blocks before the Scheduler Management section. Change the Register comment: 'in-memory H2' is no longer true, because the user now lives in the shared middleware jwt_user table (technical_gaps).

Stage A: change 'implements ApiApi' to 'implements EmailApi' and the import com.alramz.api.ApiApi to com.alramz.api.EmailApi. Nothing else changes. A grep of src/ shows that this file holds the only 2 references to ApiApi. EmailControllerTest does not reference it.
Stage D: add SmsProperties.class to @EnableConfigurationProperties. Stage E: add @EnableScheduler(jobGroupName = "notification") (import com.alramz.scheduler.EnableScheduler).

Stage C: add @ExceptionHandler(TemplatedEmailException.class) with a switch on the code: EML001-006 → 400 with code+msg; EML007 → 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE with code+msg; EML008 → 429 with code+msg; EML009 → 502 and EML010/default → 500, both with null codes and logged (code + correlationId only). Stage D: add @ExceptionHandler(SmsException.class): SMS001-005/007 → 400 and SMS008 → 404, both with code+msg; SMS009 → 502, SMS010 → 503 and SMS011/default → 500, with null codes and logged without the exception message or cause. Keep the existing arms and the single @Order(0) advice; no second advice bean (exception-handling.md pitfall). The catch-all's log text is left unchanged (the spec makes the change optional, so it is skipped).

Stage C: also register the size interceptor for /api/v1/email/template/send. On that path it throws TemplatedEmailException("EML007", "Attachments size limit exceeded"), and /api/v1/email/send keeps EmailValidationException MGE-V-008. Implement this as a second small interceptor built from the same limit (a factory taking a Supplier<RuntimeException>), with no URI branching.

RuntimeException carrying String code, in the EmailValidationException shape. Constructors (code, message) and (code, message, cause). No HttpStatus inside (exception-handling.md).

Hand-written record (not generated) for one email_configurations row: id, templateName, numberOfPlaceholders, maxAttempts, fromEmail, enSubject, arSubject, enBody, arBody, attachmentsMaxSize (String), numberOfAttachments (Integer), typeOfAttachments, bulk (boolean).
Hand-written record for one email_log insert: templateId, to, cc, bcc, bodySha256, language, dateTime (LocalDateTime), invoker, ipAddress, attachmentsMetaData.

Concrete @Repository, no interface. Injects @Qualifier("middlewareNamedParameterJdbcTemplate") and SqlQueriesManager (MmfRepositoryImpl style). Methods: Optional<EmailTemplate> findByName(String); int countSentToday(templateId, invoker, toOrNull, dayStart, dayEnd), choosing the bulk or per-recipient key; void insertLog(EmailLogEntry).

Concrete @Service, no interface: one implementation, and the only caller is the controller. Runs spec 3.1 steps 1-12 in order: collect field checks → EML001; findByName → EML002; placeholders → EML003; attachments (count EML004, type/fileName/extension EML005/EML006, decoded size EML007, bad attachments_max_size EML010); daily limit on the Asia/Dubai day → EML008; render (HtmlUtils.htmlEscape the placeholder values when the stored body starts with '<' after strip; null subject/body → EML010); MIME mapping; build com.alramz.model.EmailRequest and call EmailService#sendEmail; map gateway exceptions (EmailServiceException → EML009, which per spec 3.1 step 9 is not attached as a cause; V-008 → EML007; V-004 → EML004; other V-codes → EML010); insertLog in try/catch (log and still return 200); one structured log line holding counts only. The email regex is copied as a constant with a comment pointing at EmailServiceImpl, which stays untouched (spec scope). Invoker comes from ObjectProvider<JwtContext> → getCurrentApplication() or "unknown". The IP comes from LoggingHelper.extractClientIp(HttpServletRequest), with the request passed in by the controller. A public constructor uses Clock.system(Asia/Dubai); a package-private constructor takes a Clock (MmfServiceImpl precedent, so no Clock bean).

@RestController implements the generated TemplatedEmailApi. sendTemplatedEmail is @JwtSecured(roles = "APP_NOTIFICATION"), with no @Loggable. It delegates to TemplatedEmailService (passing the injected HttpServletRequest for the IP) and returns the 200 GenericResponse + EmailSendResult{correlationId}, like EmailController.

Record @ConfigurationProperties("app.sms"), following the local EmailProperties record precedent. Nested records: Defaults(msgCategory, expiryInSecs, contentType, sender, priority), Etisalat(baseUrl, username, password, excludedPrefixes List, excludedCountryCodes List), Waselney(sendUrl, reportUrl, username, password), Veriphone(baseUrl, apiKey), and Stage E's Dispatch(enabled, batchSize, Status(pending, inProgress, invalidMobile Integer nullable; sent, failed)). Top-level fields: liveSendEnabled, preferredProvider, maxRecipients, maxMessageLength, connectTimeout and readTimeout (Duration). The compact constructor holds the fail-fast checks E45 (live-send credentials) and E44 status rules (all set, 5 distinct, pending not 88/1). Null nested records are defaulted, so tests can build instances cheaply. toString must not print passwords/apiKey: override toString on Etisalat/Waselney/Veriphone to redact them.
RuntimeException carrying String code. Constructor (code, message); deliberately no cause constructor, so credential-bearing exception messages are never chained (spec section 5).

The cross-feature interface for notification-otp. It declares 'Outcome sendWithOutcome(SmsSendRequest)', with a nested 'record Outcome(SmsSendResult result, boolean anyProviderRejected)', and 'default SmsSendResult send(SmsSendRequest r) { return sendWithOutcome(r).result(); }'. The extra method exists because the spec needs SMS009-vs-SMS010 in the controller and 500|-vs-503| in the dispatch job, but SmsRecipientResult carries no failure reason (spec gap, technical_gaps). It does not change the public contract.

@Service implementing SmsService. Validates in spec order (SMS001, 003, 004, 002 with a 1-based entry index, 005) after splitting on [;,/\s]+, stripping one '+' and de-duplicating in order. The router follows spec 3.2: preferred provider, then excluded prefixes, then VeriPhone country_code, with a VeriPhone failure routing to Etisalat. Waselney numbers are sent first, then Etisalat, collecting one SmsRecipientResult per number. Simulated mode (live-send-enabled=false) is handled HERE, so the client beans are never called (zero HTTP). Clients return a messageId or throw SmsException SMS009 (rejected) / SMS010 (transport); the router catches each one per number, marks the number FAILED and sets anyProviderRejected. Numbers are masked to the last 4 digits in logs.

@Component. Login is POST {base}/login/user, with the token + expiry cached in a volatile field, refreshed within 60 s of decodedValue.expiryDt or once on a 401 from send. Send is POST {base}/campaigns/submissions/sms/nb with the spec body; expiryDt is UTC, formatted yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'; clientTxnId = correlationId. A 201 returns jobId, falling back to the recipient. No transport retry. The RestClient is built with the static RestClient.builder() (NOT the Boot-managed RestClient.Builder bean) plus a SimpleClientHttpRequestFactory with the app.sms timeouts. A package-private constructor takes a RestClient.Builder for MockRestServiceServer.bindTo in tests.

@Component. send(number, msg): UCS-2 hex encoding, a GET built with UriComponentsBuilder (encoded query), and a '1701|id|...' response → id, anything else → SmsException SMS009. report(messageId): GET report-url?uname&pwd&usertype=0&id, parsed with a DocumentBuilderFactory hardened (disallow-doctype-decl, external entities off, FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING) into List<Map<String,String>> from DeliveryReport/DeliveryReport/Report. 'There is no record(s) found' or zero Reports → SMS008; unparseable or non-2xx → SMS009; transport → SMS010. Catch RestClientException / ResourceAccessException and log only the provider, the exception class name and the status; never the message, URI or cause. RestClient construction is the same as in EtisalatSmsClient.

@Component. Optional<String> countryCode(number) calls POST {veriphone.base-url}/v2/verify?key=&phone= (onboarding PhoneValidationServiceImpl precedent). Any failure → Optional.empty(), logged with the exception class only (the key is in the query string). RestClient construction is the same as in EtisalatSmsClient.

@RestController implements the generated SmsApi. sendSms and getSmsReport are each @JwtSecured(roles = "APP_NOTIFICATION"), with no @Loggable. sendSms calls smsService.sendWithOutcome. If no result is SENT it throws SmsException(anyProviderRejected ? "SMS009" : "SMS010"); otherwise it returns 200 GenericResponse{response=SmsSendResult}. getSmsReport validates messageId against ^[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,65}$ (SMS007). In simulated mode it returns SMS008 without a call; otherwise it calls WaselneySmsClient.report and returns SmsReportResult. The report logic stays in the controller plus the client, with no extra service class (one caller, a few lines). Move it into SmsServiceImpl only if the reviewer insists on a thin controller.

Concrete @Repository with @ConditionalOnProperty(prefix="company.datasource", name="brok.enabled", havingValue="true"). It injects @Qualifier("brokNamedParameterJdbcTemplate"), @Qualifier("brokTransactionManager") (wrapped in a TransactionTemplate) and SqlQueriesManager. claimPending(int batchSize, int pending, int inProgress) runs sms.claim.select plus sms.claim.markInProgress inside ONE transactionTemplate.execute, using a plain jdbc.query and no maxRows/fetchSize mutation of the shared brok template. markResult(serialNo, status, messageId (truncated to 65), sendDate, incrementAttempts, inProgress) runs the guarded update. It holds a nested record SmsTableRow(long serialNo, String messageBody, String mobileNo, Integer sendAttempts); MOBILE_NO is read via getBigDecimal().toPlainString().

@Component("smsDispatchJobRunner") implements Schedulable (howto location). It takes ObjectProvider<SmsTableRepository>, SmsService, SmsProperties and a Clock (two-constructor pattern). The constructor throws IllegalStateException when dispatch.enabled=true and the repository bean is absent (that is, brok is disabled; E44). run(): return at once if dispatch is disabled. Otherwise claim; for each row put a fresh MDC correlationId and map the outcomes per spec 3.4 (invalid mobile / SENT 200|id|cid|provider / FAILED 500| or 503| from Outcome.anyProviderRejected / row exception 503|cid|NONE). Log one summary line per run. A whole-body try/catch means run() never throws, and the MDC is cleared in finally.

test_files.covers: Stage B/E context load: add company.datasource.middleware.enabled=true, url jdbc:h2:mem:notification;MODE=PostgreSQL;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1, driverClassName org.h2.Driver, username sa, plainPassword sa, startup-validation.enabled=false and spring.liquibase.change-log=classpath:db/changelog/test/db.changelog-master.yaml to the properties array. This proves 001-003 apply on H2, DatasourceConfiguration/@EnableScheduler wire up, SmsDispatchJob is creatable with brok off, and SmsProperties binds with both flags false (nothing checked). Acceptance criterion: the 3 new paths are not in permit-all-urls in any of the 6 files. Extend doesNotContain to /api/v1/email/template/send, /api/v1/sms/send and /api/v1/sms/report/** (and the /{messageId} form). Baseline: the dev case already fails today because of the working-tree ${JWT_SECRET:default...} (spec section 9 item 18). Record it; do not fix it here.

TemplatedEmailException EML001-006 → 400, EML007 → 413, EML008 → 429 with codes; EML009 → 502 and EML010 → 500 with null codes. SmsException SMS001-005/007 → 400 and SMS008 → 404 with codes; SMS009 → 502, SMS010 → 503 and SMS011 → 500 with null codes. The existing AccessDenied → 403 null-code test covers E2 for the new endpoints.
E12 Content-Length branch: the template path throws TemplatedEmailException EML007, the send path keeps MGE-V-008. Update registersInterceptorOnSendPathOnly to expect both registrations.
Direct construction (no MockMvc): 200 envelope with the MDC correlationId; @JwtSecured roles == APP_NOTIFICATION by reflection (EmailControllerTest precedent).

E5-E19 with exact codes and errorMsg text; one success test per MIME row of the 3.1 table; %1%/%2% replaced at every occurrence; HTML escaping (E19); bulk vs per-recipient count query and Dubai-day bounds from a fixed Clock (E14/E15); exactly one insertLog with the SHA-256 hex, the attachments_meta_data shape or {}, invoker 'unknown' when JwtContext is null, and the clock dateTime; no insert on any failure path; E18 insert throws → still OK; a ListAppender proves that no address, placeholder, subject or body is logged. Mockito for EmailService and EmailTemplateRepository.

Acceptance criterion 'A test against H2 proves countSentToday + insertLog + findByName SQL runs on the 002 schema'. Plain JUnit: DriverManagerDataSource jdbc:h2:mem:...;MODE=PostgreSQL, ScriptUtils runs classpath db/changelog/test/sql/002-notification-email-tables.sql (the Liquibase header and rollback lines are SQL comments), and SqlQueriesManager uses a MockEnvironment with sql.file. Covers the bulk and per-recipient counts and the day boundaries.

E20-E27 and E32: validation order and messages; de-duplication; simulated mode → every number SENT, simulated=true, verifyNoInteractions on all 3 clients; the routing matrix (non-ETISALAT → Waselney; empty prefixes → Etisalat; prefix plus an excluded country → Waselney, a non-excluded one → Etisalat; VeriPhone empty → Etisalat; Waselney called before Etisalat via InOrder); anyProviderRejected for mixed and all-transport failures.

E28/E29 (all FAILED → SMS009 if any rejection, else SMS010); 200 on a partial failure (E27); E33 messageId 'abc&pwd=x' → SMS007; E34 simulated report → SMS008 with no client call; @JwtSecured on both methods by reflection.

MockRestServiceServer.bindTo(builder): expiryDt in UTC with the .SSS'Z' format; 201 → jobId; one 401 → exactly one re-login and one re-send (E30); two 401s → SMS009 (E31); token reused until within 60 s of expiry; a ResourceAccessException → SMS010 with the password absent from logs.

'Hi ع' → 0048006900200639; an encoded query; 1701|123|x → '123', otherwise SMS009; report: two Reports → two maps; a DOCTYPE in the response → SMS009 (E35); 'There is no record(s) found' → SMS008 (E34); a timeout → SMS010 (E36); a ListAppender proves no query string or password appears in logs even when the ResourceAccessException message contains the URL.
country_code parsed; transport or 5xx failure → Optional.empty(); the API key and the URL query string are never logged.

E45: live-send-enabled=true without the Waselney creds, without the Etisalat creds when preferred=ETISALAT, or without the VeriPhone key when prefixes are non-empty → IllegalStateException. E44 status part: dispatch enabled with a missing, duplicate or 88/1 pending status → throws. Both flags false → nothing checked. toString redacts secrets.

E38 (flag off → the repository provider is never touched); E40-E42 (exact status, MESSAGE_ID format, 65-character truncation, incrementAttempts and the inProgress guard passed to markResult); E43 (a claim exception, or one row's exception, does not escape run() and the other rows are still processed); E44 brok part (dispatch enabled and the repository bean absent → the constructor throws).

The claim SQL in sql-queries.xml contains FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and a ROWNUM bound, and does NOT contain FETCH FIRST. claim select and markInProgress run inside one TransactionTemplate (mocked PlatformTransactionManager: getTransaction once, commit once). markResult SQL contains AND STATUS = :inProgressStatus. This cannot prove Oracle lock semantics (see technical_gaps).

execution_steps: BASELINE (before any edit): run 'mvn -pl services/alramz-notification-service -am clean test' and record the result. ProfileSecurityConfigTest[application-dev.yml] is expected to fail already, because the working-tree dev yml has ${JWT_SECRET:defaultSecret...} (spec section 9 item 18). Do not attribute that failure to this feature, and do not fix it here.

STAGE A, codegen fix (independently verifiable). Step 1: pom.xml: move <useTags>true</useTags> to be a direct child of <configOptions> and delete <tags>. Step 2: EmailController: 'implements EmailApi' plus the import. Step 3: grep -r ApiApi services/alramz-notification-service/src → 0 hits. Verify with 'mvn -pl services/alramz-notification-service -am clean test-compile'. clean is REQUIRED, because the stale target/generated-sources/.../ApiApi.java would otherwise survive. Then run test: everything except the baseline failure stays green, and target/generated-sources/openapi/src/main/java/com/alramz/api/EmailApi.java exists while ApiApi.java does not.

STAGE B, persistence foundation (no feature code yet). Step 4: pom.xml dependencies: liquibase starter, postgresql/ojdbc11/orai18n runtime, h2 → test. Step 5: config/DatasourceConfiguration.java (verbatim from wealth). Step 6: the 5 db.changelog-master.yaml files, plus 001-notification-schedule-job.sql and 002-notification-email-tables.sql copied byte-identically into all 5 sql/ folders. Step 7: in the 5 profile yml files, replace the H2 spring.datasource block with spring.liquibase.change-log plus company.datasource.middleware (plus cipher.password in preprod/prod); add sql.file to application.yml. Step 8: sql/sql-queries.xml with the 4 email.* keys. Step 9: AlramzNotificationServiceApplicationTests properties (middleware on H2 MODE=PostgreSQL plus the test change-log). Verify with test-compile, then test: contextLoads proves 001/002 apply on H2 and the JPA/JWT wiring still starts on the @Primary middleware DataSource.

STAGE C, templated-email slice (depends on A and B only; independently testable). Step 10: openapi.yaml path /api/v1/email/template/send plus the TemplatedEmailRequest/TemplateAttachment schemas and the generalised GenericResponse descriptions; pom modelsToGenerate += TemplatedEmailRequest,TemplateAttachment. Step 11: TemplatedEmailException plus its GlobalExceptionHandler arm. Step 12: the model records EmailTemplate and EmailLogEntry; EmailTemplateRepository. Step 13: TemplatedEmailService. Step 14: TemplatedEmailController (implements TemplatedEmailApi). Step 15: RequestSizeLimitConfig template path → EML007. Step 16: apiCollection.http templated blocks plus the Register comment fix; ProfileSecurityConfigTest template path. Step 17: tests TemplatedEmailServiceTest, TemplatedEmailControllerTest, EmailTemplateRepositoryTest, plus the GlobalExceptionHandlerTest/RequestSizeLimitConfigTest additions. Verify: 'mvn -pl services/alramz-notification-service -am test'.

STAGE D, SMS send + report slice (no database; depends on A only, so it can run before or after C). Step 18: openapi.yaml paths /api/v1/sms/send and /api/v1/sms/report/{messageId} plus the 4 Sms* schemas; pom modelsToGenerate += SmsSendRequest,SmsSendResult,SmsRecipientResult,SmsReportResult (now 10). Step 19: config/SmsProperties WITHOUT the dispatch block (live-send checks only), registered in @EnableConfigurationProperties; the app.sms.* block (no dispatch) in all 6 yml files. Step 20: SmsException plus its handler arm. Step 21: EtisalatSmsClient, WaselneySmsClient (send + report) and VeriPhoneClient, each on a static RestClient.builder() with timeouts (never the Boot RestClient.Builder bean, never the starter logging interceptor). The claim select is: SELECT SERIAL_NO, MESSAGE_BODY, MOBILE_NO, SEND_ATTEMPTS FROM INSIGHT.SMS_TABLE WHERE STATUS = :pendingStatus AND SERIAL_NO IN (SELECT SERIAL_NO FROM (SELECT SERIAL_NO FROM INSIGHT.SMS_TABLE WHERE STATUS = :pendingStatus ORDER BY PRIORITY, CREATION_DATE, SERIAL_NO) WHERE ROWNUM <= :batchSize) FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. The markInProgress and markResult updates are guarded by AND STATUS = :inProgressStatus. Step 30: repository/SmsTableRepository (brok-gated, one TransactionTemplate for claim+mark). 'find services/alramz-notification-service/src -name "00?-notification-*.sql"' returns 15 files. A grep of SMS_TABLE under db/changelog finds nothing. technical_gaps.description: Oracle claim query, deliberately diverging from spec 3.4 / acceptance criterion 'claim statement sets maxRows and fetchSize to batchSize'. The spec's setMaxRows+setFetchSize approach bounds the lock set only through driver behaviour (Oracle locks SKIP LOCKED rows at fetch time, and the driver must not prefetch beyond maxRows). It also cannot be set on the shared brokNamedParameterJdbcTemplate singleton without changing the row limit of every other brok query, so it needs a PreparedStatementCreator or a private JdbcTemplate: more code. The well-known alternative, a ROWNUM top-N in an IN-subquery with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on the outer base-table query, bounds the candidate (and so the lock) set to at most batchSize in SQL itself. It keeps PRIORITY/CREATION_DATE ordering and avoids ORA-02014, because FOR UPDATE applies to the base table and not to an inline view. The trade-off: when another pod is holding the same top-N rows during its millisecond claim, this pod under-claims (possibly 0 rows) and retries on the next 15 s tick. That is safe; it never double-claims. Plain 'WHERE ROWNUM <= n FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED' was rejected, because ROWNUM is applied before both the skip and ORDER BY. Select-ids-then-lock (two statements) also works, but it is one more round trip for no extra safety. Neither H2 nor any unit test can prove Oracle lock semantics.
technical_gaps.recommendation_or_open_question: The plan uses the ROWNUM-subquery claim. At Gate review, amend acceptance criterion line 750 to: 'claim SQL contains FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and a ROWNUM bound in an IN-subquery, and no FETCH FIRST; select and in-progress update run in one brok TransactionTemplate'. If the reviewer prefers the spec's version, swap the single XML key and implement it through a PreparedStatementCreator; never mutate the shared brok template. In both cases, check with two concurrent BROKQA sessions before enabling dispatch. Assumes SERIAL_NO is unique (the spec already relies on this).

technical_gaps.description: Spec gap: the controller needs to know 'any provider rejection' (502 SMS009 vs 503 SMS010) and the dispatch job needs to know rejection vs transport (500| vs 503|), but SmsService#send returns SmsSendResult and SmsRecipientResult has no failure-reason field.
technical_gaps.recommendation_or_open_question: Resolved internally, with no public contract change: SmsService.sendWithOutcome returns record Outcome(SmsSendResult, boolean anyProviderRejected), and send() is a default method returning result(). The dispatch job sends one number per call, so the boolean is enough. The alternative was a nullable failureReason on SmsRecipientResult, which is additive but expands the public contract beyond the spec. Revisit it only if notification-otp needs the reason.

technical_gaps.description: Security near-miss not covered by the spec. The Waselney, VeriPhone and Etisalat URLs carry credentials in the query string. A RestClient built from Spring Boot's auto-configured RestClient.Builder gets ObservationRegistry instrumentation, and its client span records the full request URL. Tracing is exported via OTLP in every profile (management.tracing.sampling 1.0), so the credentials would leak into Jaeger even though no log line contains them.
technical_gaps.recommendation_or_open_question: The plan builds every SMS/VeriPhone RestClient from the static RestClient.builder(), with no observation, no customizers and no starter logging interceptor. Flag this for 04_security to confirm that no http.client span carries these URLs.

technical_gaps.description: Blast radius missed by the spec. JWT register/login (starter JwtAutoConfiguration: JPA entities jwt_user and jwt_refresh_token) currently run on this service's throwaway in-memory H2, where Hibernate auto-creates the tables. After the switch to Postgres middleware, with Liquibase present, Hibernate's ddl-auto default becomes none. register/login then read and write the SHARED jwt_user table, which onboarding-service's 002-jwt-tables.sql created (verified). So a consumer registered here is visible to every service on that DB, and vice versa. On a fresh, isolated DB the tables do not exist and login fails. contextLoads is unaffected, because nothing queries them at startup.
technical_gaps.recommendation_or_open_question: There is no code change in scope. The plan corrects the apiCollection.http Register comment. Ops/reviewer: confirm that sharing JWT consumers across services is acceptable (it already applies to every other DB-backed service). If an isolated DB is ever used, a jwt-tables changeset would be needed (out of scope).

technical_gaps.description: Shared DATABASECHANGELOG, verified facts. Liquibase identifies a changeset by (author, id, filename), and the includeAll filename is the classpath path db/changelog/<profile>/sql/<file>. onboarding-service and reference-data-service both ship db/changelog/<profile>/sql/001-schedule-job.sql with changeset gaurav:001-create-schedule-job-table. Correction to spec section 2: only that FIRST changeset is identical. Onboarding's file holds a second changeset, gaurav:002-seed-schedule-job-data (a dataValidation seed row), and reference-data's does not. No existing changelog filename contains 'notification', so the 3 new files cannot collide. Remaining risks: (1) DATABASECHANGELOGLOCK is shared, so a crashed pod's lock blocks every service's startup (existing risk). (2) CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS email_log/email_configurations silently no-ops if a differently-shaped table of the same name already exists on the shared DB. Neither name appears anywhere in the repo, but the live DB was not inspected.
technical_gaps.recommendation_or_open_question: Before the first dev deploy, check on alramz-mw-dev-db that email_log and email_configurations do not exist, and watch the first startup for lock or checksum errors.

technical_gaps.description: The Postgres null-typed bind trap. A single countSentToday query using '(:to IS NULL OR to_email = :to)' fails on Postgres ('could not determine data type of parameter') when to is null. H2 would not reveal it.

plan_critique.acceptance_criteria_coverage: full, with one deliberate amendment: the dispatch acceptance criterion 'claim statement sets maxRows and fetchSize to batchSize' is replaced by a ROWNUM-bounded IN-subquery (technical_gaps #1). Every other criterion maps to a target_files/test_files entry: contract and codegen (openapi.yaml, pom.xml, EmailController); persistence (5 masters plus 15 changesets, DatasourceConfiguration, the yml files, the context test); security (ProfileSecurityConfigTest, reflection @JwtSecured tests, the handler 403 test); config (SmsProperties plus SmsPropertiesTest); templated email E5-E19 (TemplatedEmailServiceTest, EmailTemplateRepositoryTest on H2); SMS E20-E36 (SmsServiceImplTest, SmsControllerTest, the 3 client tests including log-capture tests); dispatch E38-E44 (SmsDispatchJobTest, SmsTableRepositoryTest); manual (apiCollection.http).
blast_radius_concerns: JWT register/login move from private H2 to the shared Postgres jwt_user/jwt_refresh_token tables (the spec did not anticipate this).
First Liquibase run against a DATABASECHANGELOG and DATABASECHANGELOGLOCK shared with 5+ services. Filenames are collision-proof (verified), but the lock is shared.
schedule_job is a shared table. 001 is a no-op there, and 003 adds one row scoped to job_group_name='notification'.
The shared brokNamedParameterJdbcTemplate must not be mutated (setMaxRows/setFetchSize) for the claim. The ROWNUM design avoids touching it.
Outbound RestClient observation would put credentialed URLs into OTLP traces. Avoided by using the static RestClient.builder().
GlobalExceptionHandler is the single advice for all controllers. The new arms are additive, and existing arms and log text are unchanged.
The useTags fix renames the generated interface for every path. Only EmailController referenced ApiApi (verified).
plan_critique.notes: The weakest part is still the dispatch claim. Switching to the ROWNUM top-N subquery removes the dependence on the JDBC driver's prefetch and maxRows behaviour, and on mutating a shared template. But correctness under concurrent pods still rests on Oracle SKIP LOCKED semantics that no test in this repo can exercise, so a manual two-session check against BROKQA is required before SMS_DISPATCH_ENABLED is ever turned on. Dispatch ships disabled, so this does not gate merge. Second weakest: the three provider protocols are implemented from prose only, and the first shared-DB Liquibase rollout needs to be watched.

focused_reviews.size_and_staging: There are 49 new and 17 modified files: 38 new main files, 20 of them changelog copies (5 masters + 3 SQL files × 5 folders), plus 11 new tests. The steps are ordered A (codegen fix) → B (persistence foundation) → C (templated email) → D (SMS send/report) → E (dispatch job). Each stage ends with a test run. C and D both depend only on A (D does not need B), so either slice can be built and verified alone, and a failure in one does not block the other. Stage E is last, because it alone needs brok, the scheduler and 003. The cost of staging is that openapi.yaml, pom.xml, the yml files and GlobalExceptionHandler are each edited 2-3 times. This is accepted for incremental verification.
focused_reviews.oracle_claim: See technical_gaps #1. The plan recommends and adopts the IN (SELECT ... WHERE ROWNUM <= n over an ordered inline view) + FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED pattern. It is simpler than the spec's version (a plain jdbc.query, with no PreparedStatementCreator or private JdbcTemplate), bounds the lock set in SQL, and keeps ordering. Plain ROWNUM+SKIP LOCKED in one query block was rejected (ROWNUM is applied before both the skip and ORDER BY). Select-ids-then-lock was rejected as an extra round trip with no gain. Unit tests can only assert the SQL text and the transaction boundary.
focused_reviews.scheduler: The starter scheduler is required by repo convention, not over-built. scheduler-jobs.md explicitly forbids plain @Scheduled, and both shipping jobs (reference-data-service, onboarding-service) use @EnableScheduler plus a schedule_job row. The incremental cost is small, because the middleware datasource is being enabled anyway for the email tables: one annotation, one INSERT changeset (×5), and the IF-NOT-EXISTS schedule_job DDL (×5, a no-op on the shared DB but needed for H2 and fresh DBs). Verified: SchedulerConfiguration hard-requires @Qualifier("middlewareNamedParameterJdbcTemplate"), JobScheduleManager reads 'schedule_job WHERE job_group_name=:g AND enable='Y'', and FIXED_DELAY calls scheduleWithFixedDelay(runnable, delay-in-ms). If the schedule_job query throws, schedule() swallows it and schedules nothing (silently), which is another reason to ship 001. A considered but rejected shortcut: the YAML fallback company.scheduler.jobs[] would drop 001 and 003 (10 files), but the howto calls DB rows the source of truth, and the ops refresh endpoint reads the DB. The 'company.scheduler.pool-size/thread-*' entries in 5 profile files are cosmetic (the pool starts threads lazily), so they are flagged under speculative additions.
focused_reviews.use_tags: Verified: <useTags> is currently nested inside a bogus <tags> element in pom.xml (lines 195-197), so only ApiApi is generated (target/generated-sources/.../api/ApiApi.java exists). After the fix, the interfaces are EmailApi (tag Email), TemplatedEmailApi and SmsApi. A grep of services/alramz-notification-service/src finds ApiApi only in EmailController.java (the import and the implements clause), and both are updated in Stage A. No test references it. Use 'clean' so the stale ApiApi.java is removed.
speculative_additions: app.sms.defaults.content-type / sender / priority, and dispatch.status.sent (88) / failed (1), are configurable values that never change. They could be constants, which would also simplify the distinctness check. No acceptance criterion requires them to be configurable (the criteria only require that pending/in-progress/invalid-mobile have no default).

app.sms.* is duplicated in all 6 yml files, and company.scheduler.* in 5. Every value is an identical env placeholder, so application.yml alone would do. The acceptance criteria require 'All 6 yml files define app.sms.*', so the plan follows them. Recommend amending that criterion to drop the duplication.
The generalised GenericResponse.errorCode/response descriptions in openapi.yaml are documentation only, not in the acceptance criteria. They are kept as a one-line edit.
The GlobalExceptionHandler catch-all log-text change is optional in the spec and is NOT planned.
SMS011 has no defined throw site (E37 routes unexpected errors to the catch-all). It is mapped only through the handler's default → 500; no code throws it.
orai18n depends on the BROK character set (technical_gaps). It is kept per precedent.

SmsService is an interface with one implementation. It is kept because the spec makes it the cross-feature contract for notification-otp, matching EmailService. TemplatedEmailService, EmailTemplateRepository and SmsTableRepository are deliberately concrete classes.
A separate getReport service layer was NOT added. The controller calls WaselneySmsClient.report directly.
The liquibase-maven-plugin was NOT added (optional local CLI tooling).
